verses.text: Then we turned back and set out into the desert along the road to the Red Sea, as the LORD had told me. For a long time we wandered around the hill country of Seir.
Then the LORD said to me,
"You have wandered around this hill country long enough. Now turn north.
Give the people these orders: You are about to pass through the land of your relatives, the descendants of Esau, who live in Seir. They will be afraid of you, but be very careful.
Do not start a fight with them, because I will not give you any of their land, not even enough to put your foot on. I have given the hill country of Seir to Esau as his own.
Pay them with money for the food you eat and for the water you drink."

The LORD your God has blessed everything you have done. He has watched over you as you travelled through this huge desert. For these forty years the LORD your God has been with you, and you have not lacked anything.

So we passed by our relatives, the descendants of Esau who live in Seir. We left the Jordan Valley road that comes up from Elath and Ezion Geber, and we turned and travelled along the desert road to Moab.
The LORD said to me, "Do not trouble the Moabites or start a war with them. I will not give you any of their land, because I have given the town of Ar to the descendants of Lot as their own."
Long ago the Emim lived there. They were a strong people, many in number, and as tall as the Anakim.
Like the Anakim, they were known as Rephaim, but the Moabites called them Emim.
The Horites used to live in Seir, but the descendants of Esau drove them out. They destroyed them and settled in their place, just as Israel did in the land the LORD gave them as their own.
The LORD said, "Now get up and cross the Zered Valley." So we crossed the Zered Valley.

Thirty-eight years passed from the time we left Kadesh Barnea until we crossed the Zered Valley. By then that whole generation of fighting men had died out of the camp, as the LORD had sworn would happen.
The LORD's hand was against them until he had completely removed them from the camp.
When the last of the fighting men among the people had died,
the LORD said to me,
"Today you will pass by Ar, on the border of Moab.

When you come near the land of the Ammonites, do not trouble them or start a fight with them. I will not give you any of the Ammonites' land, because I have given it to the descendants of Lot as their own."
That land was also known as a land of the Rephaim, who used to live there. The Ammonites called them Zamzummim.
They were a strong people, many in number, and as tall as the Anakim. But the LORD destroyed them ahead of the Ammonites, who drove them out and settled in their place.
The LORD had done the same for the descendants of Esau who live in Seir. He destroyed the Horites ahead of them, and they drove them out and have lived in their place to this day.
And the Avvim, who lived in villages as far as Gaza, were destroyed by the Caphtorim, who came from Crete and settled in their place.
"Now get up and cross the Arnon Valley. Look, I am handing over to you Sihon the Amorite, king of Heshbon, and his land. Begin to take it, and go to war against him.
Starting today, I will make all the nations under heaven terrified and afraid of you. When they hear about you, they will tremble and shake with fear because of you."
From the desert of Kedemoth I sent messengers to Sihon, king of Heshbon, with an offer of peace. They said,
"Let us pass through your land. We will stay on the main road and not turn off to the right or the left.
Sell us food to eat and water to drink, and we will pay you with money. Only let us pass through on foot,
just as the descendants of Esau who live in Seir and the Moabites who live in Ar have done. Let us pass until we cross the Jordan into the land the LORD our God is giving us."
But Sihon, king of Heshbon, would not let us pass through. The LORD your God made him stubborn and his heart hard, so that he could hand him over to you, as he has now done.
The LORD said to me, "Look, I have begun to hand Sihon and his land over to you. Begin now to take over his land as your own."
Then Sihon and his whole army came out to fight us at Jahaz.
But the LORD our God handed him over to us, and we defeated him, his sons, and his whole army.
At that time we captured all his towns and completely destroyed them, the men, women, and children. We left no survivors.
We kept only the animals and the goods from the towns we had captured as plunder for ourselves.
From Aroer on the edge of the Arnon Valley, and the town in the valley itself, all the way to Gilead, no town had walls too high for us. The LORD our God gave us all of them.
But you did not go near the land of the Ammonites, the land along the Jabbok River, or the towns in the hill country, or any place the LORD our God had told us not to go.
